pages.title: File:Flickr - archer10 (Dennis) - DSCN1882B - Dennis on La Danta.jpg

ObjectName.value: Flickr - archer10 (Dennis) - DSCN1882B - Dennis on La Danta

Categories.value: Taken with Nikon Coolpix 8800|El Mirador|Flickr images reviewed by FlickreviewR|Photographs of Guatemala by Dennis G. Jarvis|2007 in El Petén|Guatemala photographs taken on 2007-02-24|Maya pyramids in Guatemala

ImageDescription.value:
This is myself on top of the largest pyramid in the world, La Danta in the Mayan site of El Mirador. Five of us each paid $700 US each to get here by helicopter and we were told that we were among the first 1000 people ever to go there.

I know these are not great shots but I thought I would share them with you.

El Mirador is a large pre-Columbian site of the Maya civilization in Guatemala. It flourished from about the 10th century BC, reaching its height from the 3rd century BC to the 2nd century AD was finally abandoned about the end of the 9th century. The site covers some 10 square miles.

The most notable structures are one is nicknamed "El Tigre", with its pyramid 180 feet high and another is called "La Danta", some 230 feet high, making it the tallest Maya structure, and one of the largest in the world, including the large platform the pyramid is set upon, an artificially built base covering some 18,000 square meters of ground, and a volume of 2,800,000 cubic meters, the largest in the world.

Although containing striking examples of Pre-Classic Maya civilization, the remote location of El Mirador has prevented it from becoming a popular tourist site.

pages.title: File:Guatemala 1828 - La Danta at the Mayan site of El Mirador (4272305705).jpg

ObjectName.value: Guatemala 1828 - La Danta at the Mayan site of El Mirador (4272305705)

Categories.value: Taken with Nikon Coolpix 8800|El Mirador|Photographs of Guatemala by Dennis G. Jarvis|2016 in El Petén|Files uploaded by Artix Kreiger|Flickr images reviewed by FlickreviewR 2|Guatemala photographs taken on 2016-04-16

ImageDescription.value:
I took a helicopter ride to reach this site, a cost of $700 US and was told I was among the first 1000 people to visit the place. As you can see the site is covered in rain forest. It use to take two days on a donkey to reach the site and two days back. It was expensive but a highlight of my life.

View of La Danta pyramid, it is the largest Maya temple ever built. The temple reaches 79 metres (259 ft) high, and with a volume of 2,800,000 cubic meters, it is one of the largest pyramids, if not the largest, in the world. I climbed to the top and had to use a rope to pull myself up at times, no steps at that time. La Danta is considered by some archeologists to be one of the most massive ancient structures in the world.

In 2003, Dr. Richard D. Hansen, a Senior Scientist from Idaho State University, initiated major investigation, stabilization, and conservation programs at El Mirador with a multi-disciplinary approach, including staff and technical personnel from 52 universities and research institutions from throughout the world.

El Mirador flourished from about the 6th century BC, reaching its height from the 3rd century BC to the 1st century AD, with a population of perhaps more than a hundred thousand people. It then experienced a hiatus of construction and perhaps abandonment for generations, followed by re-occupation and further construction in the Late Classic era, and a final abandonment about the end of the 9th century. The civic center of the site covers some 10 square miles (26 km2) with several thousand structures, including monumental architecture from 10 to 30 meters high.
